title: Zero-stake periods burn emission schedule against no stakers, stranding budget when stake returns to zero mid-window

classification.assetImpact: Effective runway shorter than nominal windowDuration when totalStaked == 0 for a material fraction of the window. Budget remains on-contract (not stranded unrecoverable) but the intended 'emit over windowDuration of staking' interpretation is violated.
attackPath: 1. Owner sets windowDuration and funds rewardBudget; windowEnd = t0 + windowDuration.
2. No stakers deposit for a material fraction of the window (e.g. 81 days).
3. _updatePool observations advance lastRewardTime but windowEnd is not extended.
4. First staker arrives to find effective runway of (windowEnd - now), shorter than windowDuration.
5. Either owner calls setWindowDuration to re-anchor, or non-owner triggers pullAndRefresh with non-zero inflow.
classification.likelihood: low - requires deployment/fund sequence with an empty gap before first staker.
classification.assumptions: windowEnd is interpreted as wall-clock (implementation) vs 'staking time' (spec intuition).
classification.externalRequirements: Deployment ordering where fund happens before any staker deposits and stake does not arrive promptly.

justification: Low/QA. Spec-intent vs implementation divergence. No permissionless exploit; effect requires an unusual lifecycle (extended zero-stake period). Fund is not permanently lost - owner can re-anchor via setWindowDuration. QA-tier observation best handled in the Low/QA bundle with a documentation or code-level fix.
